title: EnrolledAuthenticator
description: One of the caller's enrolled factors, derived from identity_domain::authenticator::Authenticator. The domain type is the fact of ENROLMENT — which factor, for whom, since when, whether it has been used — and deliberately holds no secret: the TOTP seed, the recovery codes and the passkey public key are identity-security's business. That is what lets the domain answer 'what may this user present?' without touching a secret, and it is why this type is safe to hand to a browser. Note the two gaps against the Rust type, which are load-bearing and are recorded below: `last_used_at_ms` and `user_id` are NOT in this view.
x-rust-type: identity_domain::authenticator::Authenticator, projected — the user_id is implied by the session and is not re-sent
x-serde-status: the domain type is IMPLEMENTED; the projection has no Rust type of its own, and no route serves it
x-projection-note: The Rust Authenticator carries six fields. The self-service view carries four: user_id is redundant on a route that reads the caller's own account, and last_used_at_ms is a step-up window input that the UI does not read. A view that carried either would be disclosing session state to a browser for no gain. The projection is therefore a contract-level decision, not a serde derivation, and it is stated here rather than left to be discovered by a client.

authenticator_id.description: This enrolment's identifier. A handle used to address the enrolment in a removal request; it is not a credential and does not authenticate anything.

kind.description: What kind of factor this is. email_otp is a first factor (AuthenticatorKind::is_primary_factor); totp and passkey are second factors (is_second_factor); recovery_code is neither — it is a single-use secret for when every other factor is lost.

x-accepted-values.constraining: an enum in Rust; the wire values are the snake_case variant names

label.description: A user-chosen label, so two authenticator apps are distinguishable. Bounded at 200 bytes by Authenticator::with_label. NOT nullable in this view: a label is required for a row to be useful to a user looking at a list, and Authenticator.label is Option<String> in the domain precisely so the domain can represent 'never labelled' while the self-service view presents an empty string as '' rather than null.
label.x-serde: Authenticator.label (as a non-null string in the projection)
label.x-divergence-from-domain: Authenticator.label is Option<String>. This view types it as a required string, defaulting an absent label to the empty string. A consumer must not treat an empty label as a display bug; it is the projection's choice, and the alternative — a null the UI would have to special-case — carries no more information.

enrolled_at_ms.description: When it was enrolled, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

x-fields-deliberately-absent.user_id: implied by the session; the route reads the caller's own account and re-sending it would be noise
x-fields-deliberately-absent.last_used_at_ms: the step-up window input (Authenticator::was_used_recently) is a server-side authorization decision, not a field a browser reads
x-fields-deliberately-absent.secret_material: the TOTP seed, recovery codes and passkey public key are not on this type at all — that is the point of Authenticator's design, and a field carrying any of them would be a finding

x-phase: Phase 3 — Second factor, and the assurance model for the authenticator; Phase 5 — Applications, grants, and the self-service surface for the screen that renders it
